description:
Base 12: build on Base 11 (v311_generalist_motor_choice) with the STS3215 (motor_sts 1) as the motor. Jake's feedback on Base 11, now that we have the smaller motor:
1. Remove the small piece that sticks out into the central gripping area between the fingers. Keep the center as clear as possible, since objects get gripped there. The four corner connection points are enough.
2. Shrink the gearbox area significantly, by about half, so it doesn't extend far over the forearm.
3. Mount the motor flush with the bottom of the gripper, right there, and re-gear from that position, e.g. one larger gear on the motor driving smaller gears on each finger, or whatever is most compact.
Keep it parameterized, printable without supports, and keep the strap slots clear.

results.identified_issue: Base 12 = v312_generalist_compact_drive, copied from v311, STS3215 only (motor_sts pinned 1..1; the RS00 code paths and wrist-mount asserts remain but are guarded by sts and unused; the RS00 50 mm screw ring cannot fit base_r 17.5). Pivot: gripper.scad pivot=pivot_spacing/2 (new param, Gears group). reach = Base 11's derived half-spacing. toe = least plan rotation that brings any outline point to the centreline: min over outline points of atan2(z,r)-acos(pivot/R). placed() rotates by s*(a-toe); gear_solid counter-rotates teeth+fan by rotate(-toe) so teeth stay square to the pivots' line (pinion phase/teeth_span unchanged); rib2d uses rotate(toe-a). contact_back recalibrated to -0.017: with toe the solid meets 0.6 mm behind the traced point where tip rounding sits 0.019 mm out; at -0.017 the closed gap is ~0.002 mm/side (contact positive control pushes 0.01). If pivot_spacing is changed on the Tune slider, contact_back may need re-tuning by a few microns for the touch/positive-control checks to both pass; the geometry itself still meets. check_geometry gap_profile now reads rotate([0,-toe]) whole_finger() and opens the Gen 14 target by 2*d*tan(toe). Pinion: pinion_teeth 16 (fewest with horn csk heads 1 mm inside roots at the larger 1.84 module), pin_c placed by pinion_mesh_deg 55 from the right pivot (under ~53 deg its tip enters the left gear's swept teeth). Pillars: pillar_x/pillar_z replace pillar_pin_r/pillar_deg/pillar_top_z; third pillar and centre tab removed from base_outline and top2d. sts_body_deg 90: servo entirely inside the base outline; hump window becomes an internal slot (genus base still 7). Results: 59/59 geometry checks, genus pass, meshes single-component. Lowest point -55.3 (Base 11 -82.4); width 85 (77). Not half because gear pitch radius = pivot half-spacing grows with the 15% wider spacing. Interpretation risk: 'flush with the bottom' read as 'inside the base outline, nothing hanging below'; the servo is still on the ventral face (adds ~32 mm thickness as in Base 11). Pre-existing failures not touched: Scripts/test_gripper_poses.py (v306 has no poses entry) and check_gripper_closure.py ('never touches' on every Base).
results.summary: Made Base 12: wider finger spacing as a slider, nothing between the fingers, a much smaller gearbox, and the STS3215 tucked under the base.
results.detailed_description:
Base 12 is up (v312). The new pivot_spacing slider sets how far apart the finger bases are. It's at 62.7 mm, 15% wider than Base 11. Each finger tilts in about 1.9° so the tips still meet at a point, and the gap at the base is wider. The gears, pinion and base all resize from that one number.

The pillar on the tab between the fingers is gone. The top plate now stands on two corner pillars and is held at the top by the two rings round the pivots. The pinion went from 34 to 16 teeth and sits just off the centreline. That's a 2.1:1 reduction, so the servo turns 64° for 30° of finger swing, which gives more grip torque. The servo's body now points up under the base instead of hanging below it, so nothing sticks out past the base.

The bottom is now 55 mm below the pivots (Base 11: 82), and the whole drive is 69 mm tall (Base 11: 113). It's not quite half because the wider spacing makes the side gears bigger. All 59 geometry checks pass and every part still prints without supports. Nothing has been printed yet. I read "flush with the bottom" as the servo sitting fully inside the base outline. It is still on the back face, so it adds the same thickness as before; tell me if you meant something else.

summary: Redesign the Base 12 gripper around the STS3215 motor mounted flush at the bottom, with a halved gearbox and a clear center. Re-gear compactly, such as one large motor gear driving smaller finger gears, while staying parameterized and printable without supports.
